visual: Mound-forming deciduous Japanese maple with graceful arching branches and finely dissected lace-like foliage. Leaves emerge orange-red in spring, deepen to reddish-green through summer and turn vivid orange-red again in autumn.
water: Keep evenly moist during establishment and water during prolonged dry periods, particularly when container grown.
aspect: Partial shade to full sun; sheltered
soil: Fertile, moist but well-drained acid to neutral soil.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging, severe drought and exposed windy positions. Delicate foliage can scorch where soil becomes dry or plants receive excessive hot sun.
prune: Requires little routine pruning. Remove dead, damaged or unwanted branches during dormancy and avoid heavy pruning.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very cold hardy but the fine foliage is vulnerable to wind scorch and moisture stress.
uses: Japanese gardens, specimen planting, courtyards, rock gardens, banks, slopes and containers.
foliage: Deciduous; finely cut orange-red spring leaves becoming reddish-green in summer before turning brighter orange-red in autumn.
container: Excellent slow-growing Japanese maple for a large container where moisture can be kept consistent.
uncertain: Nursery labels may write Acer palmatum 'Dissectum Orangeola' or Acer palmatum var. dissectum 'Orangeola'. RHS currently lists Acer palmatum var. dissectum 'Orangeola' as a synonym and recognises the cultivar as Acer palmatum 'Orangeola' in the Dissectum horticultural group.
peak "Spring and autumn foliage" converted to "Sep-Nov" to parse as Mon-Mon.

visual: Clump-forming herbaceous peony with glossy dark green divided foliage and large, fragrant, richly coloured flowers. The blooms combine deep carmine, dark magenta-red to purple outer petals with a contrasting creamy centre, becoming increasingly full as mature plants develop.
water: Water regularly during establishment and during prolonged dry periods. Established plants prefer consistent moisture but should not remain waterlogged.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade; sheltered position preferred
soil: Deep, fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged soil and do not plant the crown too deeply, as deep planting can significantly reduce flowering.
prune: Remove spent flowers as they fade. Cut stems and foliage back to near ground level as the plant dies down in autumn.
toxicity: May cause skin irritation in pets.
hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe, approximately -20 to -15°C.
resilience: Very hardy, long-lived herbaceous perennial that can remain productive for decades when planted correctly and left relatively undisturbed.
uses: Herbaceous borders, cottage gardens, mixed borders, specimen planting and cut-flower gardens.
foliage: Deciduous herbaceous foliage; glossy dark green divided leaves emerge in spring and die completely back in autumn.
container: Can be grown in a very large, deep container, although long-term performance is generally better in open ground.
uncertain: The American Peony Society records 'Tom Cat' as a Lactiflora cultivar registered by R. G. Klehm in 2000 and notes that it may be the same plant as 'Spiffy' because of similar seedling numbers and flower characteristics.
